speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned a generalized nonpruritic rash, high fever, and a recent seizure. To narrow this down, can you tell me how many days the fever has been present and if you have any neck stiffness or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum) caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) or 7 (HHV-7). The clinical presentation of high fever followed by a rash after defervescence, combined with a seizure likely triggered by fever in an 9-month-old with up-to-date vaccinations, is classic for this condition.
